docs.title: pixi-policy
docs.text:
Write down what your pixi environments are allowed to contain, and check it everywhere pixi runs. One file, pixi-policy.toml, committed beside pixi.toml and pixi.lock; one command, pixi policy, that reports every package, source, license or manifest setting the policy does not allow, with the reason and a fix hint, and exits non-zero so CI can stop the merge.

pixi policy init     # write a policy the workspace passes today
pixi policy          # check it (the same as `pixi policy check`)
pixi policy explain  # every rule; `pixi policy explain <RULE>` for one, with its keys

pixi-policy reads three files and nothing else: it needs no server, no database and no network, and every check runs offline. It is a single binary that pixi runs as pixi policy.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
Family Rules Checks that Sources sources.channels, sources.indexes, sources.git, sources.url, sources.path conda packages come only from allowed channels, PyPI packages only from allowed indexes, and nothing from git, a direct URL or a local path unless allowed Bans bans.deny no banned package, version range or build is in any environment Licenses licenses.deny, licenses.review, licenses.not-allowed, licenses.unknown every package can be used under the licenses the policy allows Manifest manifest.wildcard-spec, manifest.python-pinned, manifest.required-platforms pixi.toml gives no * specs, pins Python to a minor version and lists the required platforms Lock lock.present, lock.complete, lock.in-sync pixi.lock exists, locks every environment for every platform, and still satisfies the manifest Waivers waivers.expired, waivers.unused, waivers.too-long every exception has a reason and an end date, and still matches something

Every environment and every platform in pixi.lock is checked. The rule catalog says what each rule checks, and the policy file reference lists every key with its type, allowed values and default.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
How Command From PyPI (the wheel carries only the binary) uv tool install pixi-policy, pipx install pixi-policy or pip install pixi-policy In a pixi workspace, pinned with the rest of its tools [feature.lint.pypi-dependencies] pixi-policy = ">=0.1,<0.2" in a feature that has Python, then pixi run -e lint pixi-policy A release archive download it from GitHub Releases and check where it came from with gh attestation verify <archive> --repo aesir-oss/pixi-policy

pixi finds any pixi-<name> executable on PATH, so once pixi-policy is installed pixi policy works. A conda-forge package, for pixi global install, is planned (#6).

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Nothing failed. Warnings may still be reported 1 At least one finding is an error 2 The policy, the manifest or the lockfile could not be read

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Getting started: from pixi policy init to a policy that fails the build
  • In development and CI: a pixi task, a pre-commit hook and the GitHub Action
  • Output formats: text, JSON and SARIF

docs.title: In development and CI
docs.text: The policy lives in the repository, so a laptop, a pre-commit hook and CI all check exactly the same rules. pixi-policy needs nothing running beside it: it reads pixi.toml, pixi.lock and the policy, and exits.

docs.title: What a run needs
docs.text:
• pixi.lock, committed. Every rule except the manifest ones reads it. Without a [lock] table, a missing lockfile is an input error (exit 2); with one, it is a lock.present finding.
  • pixi on PATH. lock.in-sync asks pixi, offline, whether the lockfile still satisfies the manifest (pixi list --locked). When pixi cannot be run, that check is a warning instead.
  • pixi-policy.toml, beside pixi.toml or named with --policy. A run without a policy is an error, never a pass.

docs.title: A pixi task
docs.text:
Pin pixi-policy with the workspace's other tools, in a feature that has Python, and give it a task:

# pixi.toml
[feature.lint.dependencies]
python = "3.12.*"

[feature.lint.pypi-dependencies]
pixi-policy = ">=0.1,<0.2"

[feature.lint.tasks]
policy = "pixi-policy"

[environments]
lint = { features = ["lint"], solve-group = "default" }

pixi run policy then runs the same version for everyone. Extra arguments pass through: pixi run policy --format json.

docs.title: A pre-commit hook
docs.text:
The published hook runs the check whenever pixi.toml, pixi.lock, pyproject.toml or pixi-policy.toml changes, and stops a commit with an error finding:

# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/aesir-oss/pixi-policy-pre-commit
    rev: v0.2.0
    hooks:
      - id: pixi-policy

Each tag of aesir-oss/pixi-policy-pre-commit installs the pixi-policy wheel of the same version from PyPI, so nothing is compiled; pre-commit autoupdate moves rev to the newest release. The hook checks the workspace the way pixi policy does from the repository root. args: passes any other flag: args: [--manifest-path, app/pixi.toml] for a workspace below the root.

To run the version the workspace pins instead (the pixi task above), a local hook:

# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: pixi-policy
        name: pixi policy
        entry: pixi run policy
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        files: (^|/)(pixi\.toml|pixi\.lock|pyproject\.toml|pixi-policy\.toml)$

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The GitHub Action is one step: it installs the release binary, runs the check, fails the job on an error finding and can upload the findings to code scanning.

- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action@v0
  with:
    upload-sarif: "true"

The same by hand, with the version the workspace pins: write a SARIF report and upload it, so findings appear on the pull request as code scanning annotations at the line in pixi.toml, pixi.lock or the policy. The check's exit code fails the job; if: always() uploads the report even then.

# .github/workflows/policy.yml
name: Policy
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  policy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write   # upload-sarif
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@v0.8.1
        with:
          environments: lint
      - name: Check the policy
        run: pixi run policy --format sarif --output policy.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: policy.sarif
          category: pixi-policy

Make the job a required status check, or a failing policy is only advice. Code scanning is free on public repositories; private ones need GitHub code security. Without it, drop the upload and read the text report in the job log.

docs.title: Other CI systems
docs.text: Use the exit code to pass or fail the job, and --format json --output policy.json for anything that reads the results: a dashboard, a comment bot, an artifact to keep. The JSON report has a published schema.

docs.title: Who owns the policy
docs.text: Changing pixi-policy.toml changes what the workspace may contain, so review it like code: put it under CODEOWNERS, so a new waiver or a loosened rule needs its owner's approval.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
pixi-policy is one Rust crate. Everything runs through pixi, which pins the toolchain in pixi.lock, so a checkout builds the same way on every machine and in CI.

pixi run test   # unit and end-to-end tests
pixi run ci     # the full gate: pre-commit, release build, check, clippy, coverage >= 90%

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Task What it does test cargo test: the unit tests beside the code and the end-to-end tests in tests/ lint cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings check, fmt, build cargo check, cargo fmt, the release build cov coverage with cargo llvm-cov, failing under 90% of lines ci pre-commit-run, build, check, lint and cov: what must pass before a change is done policy-docs regenerate the policy reference and the rule catalog from the code -e lint deny cargo deny check: advisories, licenses, banned crates and sources, against deny.toml -e msrv msrv-check cargo check on the oldest toolchain Cargo.toml claims -e docs docs-serve, -e docs docs-build this site, served with live reload or built strictly

pixi run bootstrap installs the pre-commit hooks once per clone.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Path What it is src/main.rs, src/cli.rs the command line src/check.rs, src/rules/ the rule engine and one module per rule family src/policy.rs, src/keys.rs the policy file's parser, and every key it accepts with its type, values and default src/lockfile.rs, src/manifest.rs, src/workspace.rs reading pixi.lock and pixi.toml src/license.rs, src/license_policy.rs, src/purl.rs license normalisation, the license verdict, package URLs src/report.rs, src/style.rs, src/pipe.rs text, JSON and SARIF reports; terminal colour; output a reader may close early src/explain.rs, src/waivers.rs, src/init.rs explain, waivers that expire, init schemas/ the JSON report's schema, published with the docs actions/pixi-policy/ the GitHub Action, copied to aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action on each release pre-commit-mirror/ the pre-commit hook, rendered into aesir-oss/pixi-policy-pre-commit on each final tests/ end-to-end tests of the binary, with fixtures and schemas examples/projects/pixi/ 19 real pixi workspaces the tests and the field test run against docs/, mkdocs.yml this site

The license, lockfile, purl, style and pipe modules began in a crate pixi-policy shared with pixi-sbom in aesir-oss/pixi-ext-contrib. Since this repository was split out, they are pixi-policy's own and change with its needs.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text: The policy reference and the rule catalog are generated from src/keys.rs and the text pixi policy explain prints. tests/docs.rs fails when either page differs from the code, and src/keys.rs has tests that fail when the policy parser accepts a key the reference does not list, or the reference lists one the parser rejects. Change the code, then run pixi run policy-docs.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
A release starts from the Release workflow (workflow_dispatch, with a version). It refuses to run unless main's CI passed on the commit, then bumps the version in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and pixi.toml, adds the release's section to CHANGELOG.md with git-cliff, commits, and pushes the tag vX.Y.Z. The tag starts Release artifacts, which builds the wheels and the five archives (pixi-policy-vX.Y.Z-<platform>), signs their provenance, publishes the GitHub release, and uploads the wheels: to TestPyPI for a release candidate (0.1.1-rc.1), to PyPI for a final. Publishing the release redeploys this site under the version.

  • Never bump versions or push tags by hand: a pushed v* tag starts a release.
  • Never edit CHANGELOG.md's existing sections. Each release adds its own on top; those up to 0.1.0 were written in aesir-oss/pixi-ext-contrib and link there.
  • Every release candidate goes through a field test of the published files before a final is cut.

The same run fills two generated repositories with the release App, which must be installed on both:

  • aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action gets actions/pixi-policy/ on every release, tagged vX.Y.Z. A final also moves vX when it is the newest release of its major, and gets a GitHub release, marked Latest when vX moved: the Marketplace lists the action from releases, not tags.
  • aesir-oss/pixi-policy-pre-commit gets the hook rendered for the version, tagged vX.Y.Z, on finals only and after the PyPI upload, since the hook installs the wheel from PyPI.

The Marketplace listing itself is a manual step, once: GitHub has no API for it. On the first final's release in aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action, choose Edit, tick Publish this Action to the GitHub Marketplace (an aesir-oss owner may first have to accept the Marketplace Developer Agreement), pick the categories Security and Continuous integration, and update the release. The listing is marketplace/actions/pixi-policy.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Start from a policy the workspace already passes, commit it, and tighten it one change at a time. Each change is then a reviewed pull request that says exactly what is no longer allowed.

docs.title: 1. Write a starting policy
docs.text:
pixi policy init

init writes pixi-policy.toml beside pixi.toml from what the workspace uses today: the channels and indexes its packages come from, every license in pixi.lock, and its platforms. It never overwrites an existing file; pass --policy <file> to write somewhere else.

# pixi-policy.toml, written by `pixi policy init` from what this workspace uses today.
[sources]
allowed-channels = ["conda-forge"]
allowed-indexes = ["https://pypi.org/simple"]
allow-git = false
allow-url = false
allow-path = false

[bans]
deny = []  # e.g. { name = "pycrypto", reason = "unmaintained", use-instead = "pycryptodome" }

[licenses]
# Every license the conda packages declare today (shortened here). pixi.lock records no PyPI licenses.
allow = ["Apache-2.0", "BSD-3-Clause", "MIT", "PSF-2.0"]
unknown = "warn"

[manifest]
required-platforms = ["linux-64", "osx-arm64", "win-64"]

[lock]  # present, complete and in-sync are all on

docs.title: 2. Check it
docs.text:
pixi policy

warning[licenses.unknown] watchdog 6.0.0: has no license in pixi.lock (it never records PyPI licenses)
  --> pixi.lock: environment "docs", win-64
  = help: PyPI licenses are read from the package's files in pixi-policy 0.2.0; until then set [licenses] unknown = "allow" to stop these

0 errors, 155 warnings, 0 waived in 1644 packages across 30 environment-platform pairs

Each finding names its rule, the package, where it was found and how to fix it. Errors fail the check (exit code 1); warnings are reported and do not. Commit pixi-policy.toml once the check passes.

docs.title: 3. Tighten it
docs.text:
Add what the workspace must never contain, one rule at a time:

[bans]
deny = [
  { name = "pycrypto", reason = "unmaintained", use-instead = "pycryptodome" },
  { name = "openssl", version = "<3", reason = "EOL" },
]

[licenses]
deny = ["GPL-3.0-*", "AGPL-*"]

pixi policy explain <RULE> says what a rule checks, gives an example and lists each of its keys with the values it takes and its default:

pixi policy explain bans.deny

docs.title: 4. Waive what has to stay, with an end date
docs.text:
When a finding cannot be fixed yet, waive that one finding with a reason and an expires date. It is reported as waived until then and fails again the day after.

[[waivers]]
rule = "licenses.deny"
package = "readline"
reason = "dev only; LEGAL-1234"
expires = 2027-03-31

See Waivers for how a waiver matches a finding.

docs.title: 5. Run it in CI
docs.text: Run the same check on every pull request, so a change to pixi.toml or pixi.lock that breaks the policy fails before it merges. In development and CI has the setup.

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action runs pixi policy check in a workflow: it downloads the release binary for the runner, verifies its checksum, runs the check and fails the job when a finding is an error. pixi itself is not needed, though with pixi on PATH (from prefix-dev/setup-pixi) the lock.in-sync rule also runs; without it, that check is a warning.

# .github/workflows/policy.yml
name: Policy
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  policy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write   # upload-sarif
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action@v0
        with:
          upload-sarif: "true"

The text report goes to the job log and the job summary. With upload-sarif, findings also appear on the pull request as code scanning annotations at the line in pixi.toml, pixi.lock or the policy. Code scanning is free on public repositories; private ones need GitHub code security. Make the job a required status check, or a failing policy is only advice.

@v0 follows the newest 0.x.y release. Pin an exact release (@v0.2.0) or a commit sha for a build that never changes underneath you; version picks the binary independently of the ref.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Default What it does version the ref's pixi-policy version to run: @v0.2.0 runs 0.2.0, @v0 the newest 0.x.y, a branch the newest release manifest-path nearest pixi.toml The workspace's pixi.toml policy pixi-policy.toml beside it The policy to check against fail-on-findings true Fail the step on an error finding; with false it passes with a warning and failed says what happened summary true Write the text report to the job summary upload-sarif false Also write the report as SARIF and upload it to code scanning (needs security-events: write) sarif-category pixi-policy Code scanning category for the upload json-output Also write the JSON report to this path extra-args Additional command-line arguments, whitespace separated

A policy, manifest or lockfile that cannot be read (exit code 2) always fails the step, whatever fail-on-findings says.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output What it is version The pixi-policy version that ran failed true when at least one finding is an error sarif Path of the SARIF report, when upload-sarif is set json Path of the JSON report, when json-output is set

docs.title: A workspace in a subdirectory
docs.text:
- uses: aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action@v0
  with:
    manifest-path: services/api/pixi.toml

Paths in the SARIF report are relative to the job's working directory, the repository root, so annotations land on the right files.

docs.title: A nightly re-check
docs.text:
When a waiver expires, the finding it waived fails the check again, with no commit to start a run. A scheduled run catches it:

on:
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *"

docs.title: Report without failing
docs.text:
- uses: aesir-oss/pixi-policy-action@v0
  id: policy
  with:
    fail-on-findings: "false"
    json-output: policy.json
- if: steps.policy.outputs.failed == 'true'
  run: echo "the workspace fails its policy; see policy.json"

docs.title: License policy with pixi-policy
docs.text:
pixi-policy's [licenses] table is the policy-file form of pixi-sbom's license gate (--allow-license, --deny-license, --require-license). Both tools evaluate a license with the same shared verdict, so a package that fails one fails the other.

# pixi-policy.toml
[licenses]
allow = ["MIT", "BSD-3-Clause", "Apache-2.0", "PSF-2.0"]
review = ["LGPL-*"]
deny = ["GPL-3.0-*", "AGPL-*"]
unknown = "warn"   # or "error", "allow"
Rule Severity Finds a package whose license… licenses.deny error cannot be satisfied without a deny license (MIT OR GPL-3.0-only passes: MIT is an option) licenses.not-allowed error cannot be satisfied with allow and review licenses alone (only when allow is given) licenses.review warning needs a review license licenses.unknown unknown is missing, or is not an SPDX expression

Entries are SPDX identifiers, or patterns with * that are expanded against the SPDX license list (LGPL-* is every LGPL identifier). An -or-later entry accepts later versions of the same license, as in pixi-sbom.

docs.title: Moving from pixi-sbom's flags
docs.text: pixi-sbom pixi-policy --allow-license MIT --allow-license Apache-2.0 [licenses] allow = ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"] --deny-license GPL-3.0-only [licenses] deny = ["GPL-3.0-only"] --require-license [licenses] unknown = "error" no --require-license [licenses] unknown = "allow" (the default, "warn", reports them without failing) --ignore-license PACKAGE:WHY a waiver with a reason and an expiry date (no equivalent) [licenses] review = [...], reported as warnings exit code 3 on a violation exit code 1 on an error finding

docs.title: What pixi-policy reads
docs.text: Licenses come from pixi.lock only, offline. It records them for conda packages and never for PyPI ones, so every PyPI package is licenses.unknown until pixi-policy 0.2.0 reads license files; set unknown = "allow" to stop those warnings meanwhile. pixi-sbom's gate also covers npm packages it reads from a package-lock.json (and licenses it fetches with --fetch-licenses); pixi-policy checks the packages in pixi.lock.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
--format picks the report: text (the default), json or sarif. --output <file> writes it to a file instead of standard output. Whatever the format, the exit code is the verdict.

Code Meaning 0 Nothing failed. Warnings may still be reported 1 At least one finding is an error 2 The policy, the manifest or the lockfile could not be read

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
For people, in a terminal or a CI log. Findings are grouped by severity, each with its rule, the package, where it was found and a fix hint, then a summary line:

error[bans.deny] openssl 3.6.4: is banned (version <3): EOL
  --> pixi.lock: environment "default", linux-64
  = help: use libressl instead

1 error, 0 warnings, 0 waived in 1644 packages across 30 environment-platform pairs

--color auto (the default) colours it when standard output is a terminal and the environment does not forbid it; always colours it even when redirected (for less -R or a CI log), and never turns colour off. A report written with --output is never coloured unless --color always.

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
For scripts and dashboards: one object per finding with stable field names, the waived findings with their waivers, and a summary.

{
  "version": 1,
  "tool": { "name": "pixi-policy", "version": "0.1.0" },
  "workspace": { "manifest": "pixi.toml", "lockfile": "pixi.lock", "policy": "pixi-policy.toml" },
  "summary": { "passed": false, "errors": 1, "warnings": 0, "waived": 0, "packages": 1644, "targets": 30 },
  "findings": [
    {
      "rule": "bans.deny",
      "severity": "error",
      "package": "openssl",
      "version": "3.6.4",
      "environment": "default",
      "platform": "linux-64",
      "file": "pixi.lock",
      "line": null,
      "message": "is banned (version <3): EOL",
      "help": "use libressl instead"
    }
  ],
  "waived": []
}

The schema is pixi-policy-report.schema.json. Fields may be added within version 1; renaming or removing one raises the version.

docs.title: SARIF
docs.text: SARIF 2.1.0, for GitHub code scanning and other SARIF viewers: one rule per rule ID, with the rule catalog's text as its help, and one result per finding at its file and line. Waived findings are included as suppressed results, so a viewer can show what was waived and why. In development and CI shows the upload.

docs.title: Policy file reference
docs.text: Every key pixi-policy.toml accepts. A key the table does not list is an error, so a misspelt key cannot quietly check nothing. pixi policy explain <RULE> prints the rows for one rule's keys.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules max-waiver-days integer 0 or more: the furthest a waiver's expires may be from today, in days; 0 turns the check off 365 no waivers.too-long

docs.title: [sources]
docs.text:
A table. When it is left out: no source rule runs.

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [sources] allowed-channels list of strings channel names or URLs. A name ("conda-forge") matches its anaconda.org and prefix.dev URLs; any other host is given by URL ("https://conda.example.com/prod"). Trailing slashes and host case do not matter not set: conda packages may come from any channel no sources.channels [sources] allowed-indexes list of strings PyPI index URLs ("https://pypi.org/simple"). Trailing slashes and host case do not matter not set: PyPI packages may come from any index no sources.indexes [sources] allow-git boolean true, false true: packages may come from a git repository no sources.git [sources] allow-url boolean true, false true: packages may come from a direct URL no sources.url [sources] allow-path boolean true, false true: packages may come from a local path no sources.path

docs.title: [bans]
docs.text:
A table. When it is left out: nothing is banned.

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [bans] deny list of tables one table per ban, with the fields below []: nothing is banned no bans.deny [bans] deny: name string a package name. A PyPI name also catches a conda package that provides it none yes bans.deny [bans] deny: version string a version range: conda's syntax for conda packages, PEP 440 for PyPI ones ("<3", ">=1.0,<1.1.1w") not set: every version is banned no bans.deny [bans] deny: build string a conda build-string pattern, with * matching any run of characters ("*_cuda*"); conda packages only not set: every build is banned no bans.deny [bans] deny: kind string "conda", "pypi" not set: both kinds no bans.deny [bans] deny: reason string any text; printed with the finding none no bans.deny [bans] deny: use-instead string any text; printed as the finding's fix hint none no bans.deny

docs.title: [licenses]
docs.text:
A table. When it is left out: no license rule runs.

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [licenses] allow list of strings SPDX license identifiers, or patterns with * expanded against the SPDX license list ("LGPL-*"). An -or-later entry accepts later versions of the same license []: any license that is not denied is acceptable no licenses.not-allowed [licenses] review list of strings SPDX license identifiers or patterns, as for allow [] no licenses.review, licenses.not-allowed [licenses] deny list of strings SPDX license identifiers or patterns, as for allow [] no licenses.deny [licenses] unknown string "warn", "error", "allow" "warn" no licenses.unknown

docs.title: [manifest]
docs.text:
A table. When it is left out: no manifest rule runs.

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [manifest] wildcard-spec boolean true, false true once the table exists; without the table the rule is off no manifest.wildcard-spec [manifest] python-pinned boolean true, false true once the table exists; without the table the rule is off no manifest.python-pinned [manifest] required-platforms list of strings pixi platform names ("linux-64", "linux-aarch64", "osx-64", "osx-arm64", "win-64", …) not set: no platform is required no manifest.required-platforms

docs.title: [lock]
docs.text:
A table. When it is left out: no lock rule runs, and a missing pixi.lock is an input error (exit 2).

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [lock] present boolean true, false true once the table exists; without the table the rule is off no lock.present [lock] complete boolean true, false true once the table exists; without the table the rule is off no lock.complete [lock] in-sync boolean true, false true once the table exists; without the table the rule is off no lock.in-sync

docs.title: [[waivers]]
docs.text:
A list of tables. When it is left out: no exceptions.

Key Type Allowed values Default Required Rules [[waivers]] rule string the ID of a policy rule, as pixi policy explain lists it ("licenses.deny"); waivers.* findings cannot be waived none yes waivers.unused [[waivers]] package string the package's name, as the finding names it (case does not matter). Findings that name no package, such as the lock rules', cannot be waived none yes waivers.unused [[waivers]] version string an exact version, as the finding names it not set: every version no waivers.unused [[waivers]] environment string an environment name from pixi.toml not set: every environment no waivers.unused [[waivers]] platform string a pixi platform name ("linux-64") not set: every platform no waivers.unused [[waivers]] reason string any text: why the exception is acceptable, and until when none yes – [[waivers]] expires date a TOML date, YYYY-MM-DD, unquoted: the last day the waiver applies none yes waivers.expired, waivers.too-long

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Every rule pixi policy check runs, with the text pixi policy explain <RULE> prints. Each rule's keys are in the policy file reference.

Rule Checks sources.channels Conda packages come only from the channels the policy allows sources.indexes PyPI packages come only from the indexes the policy allows sources.git No package comes from a git repository unless the policy allows it sources.url No package comes from a direct URL unless the policy allows it sources.path No package comes from a local path unless the policy allows it bans.deny No package, or package version, the policy bans licenses.deny No package needs a license the policy denies licenses.review Packages that need a license under review are reported for it licenses.not-allowed Every package can be used under the licenses the policy allows licenses.unknown Every package declares an SPDX license manifest.wildcard-spec No dependency is given as \* manifest.python-pinned Python is constrained to one minor version or narrower manifest.required-platforms The workspace lists every platform the policy requires lock.present The workspace has a pixi.lock lock.complete Every environment is locked for every platform it is solved for lock.in-sync pixi.lock still satisfies the manifest waivers.expired A waiver has expired, and what it waived fails again waivers.unused A waiver matches no finding waivers.too-long A waiver runs further out than max-waiver-days

docs.title: sources.channels
docs.text:
Conda packages come only from the channels the policy allows.

Key: [sources] allowed-channels, a list of channel names or URLs. A name ("conda-forge") matches its anaconda.org and prefix.dev URLs only; any other host is listed by URL. Mirrors are matched as the channel they mirror, since pixi.lock records that channel.

[sources]
allowed-channels = ["conda-forge", "https://conda.example.com/prod"]

Keys: [sources] allowed-channels.

docs.title: sources.indexes
docs.text:
PyPI packages come only from the indexes the policy allows.

Key: [sources] allowed-indexes, a list of PyPI index URLs (trailing slashes and host case do not matter). pixi.lock records a wheel's index; one from the default index is checked against it.

[sources]
allowed-indexes = ["https://pypi.org/simple"]

Keys: [sources] allowed-indexes.

docs.title: sources.git
docs.text:
No package comes from a git repository unless the policy allows it.

Key: [sources] allow-git (default: allowed). Set it to false to fail any package, conda (pixi-build) or PyPI, that comes from a git repository.

[sources]
allow-git = false

Keys: [sources] allow-git.

docs.title: sources.url
docs.text:
No package comes from a direct URL unless the policy allows it.

Key: [sources] allow-url (default: allowed). Set it to false to fail any package that comes from a direct URL: an archive, not a channel or an index.

[sources]
allow-url = false

Keys: [sources] allow-url.

docs.title: sources.path
docs.text:
No package comes from a local path unless the policy allows it.

Key: [sources] allow-path (default: allowed). Set it to false to fail any package that comes from a local path, including a workspace package pixi builds from source.

[sources]
allow-path = false

Keys: [sources] allow-path.

docs.title: bans.deny
docs.text:
No package, or package version, the policy bans.

Key: [bans] deny, a list of bans: name, and optionally version (conda's rules for conda packages, PEP 440 for PyPI ones), build (a conda build-string pattern), kind ("conda" or "pypi"), reason and use-instead. A ban on a PyPI name also catches a conda package that provides it.

[bans]
deny = [
  { name = "pycrypto", reason = "unmaintained", use-instead = "pycryptodome" },
  { name = "openssl", version = "<3", reason = "EOL" },
]

Keys: [bans] deny, [bans] deny: name, [bans] deny: version, [bans] deny: build, [bans] deny: kind, [bans] deny: reason, [bans] deny: use-instead.

docs.title: licenses.deny
docs.text:
No package needs a license the policy denies.

Key: [licenses] deny, SPDX identifiers or patterns ("GPL-3.0-*"). A package fails when its license cannot be satisfied without a denied license: MIT OR GPL-3.0-only passes, since MIT is an option. The verdict is the one pixi-sbom's --deny-license gives.

[licenses]
deny = ["GPL-3.0-*", "AGPL-*"]

Keys: [licenses] deny.

docs.title: licenses.review
docs.text:
Packages that need a license under review are reported for it.

Key: [licenses] review, SPDX identifiers or patterns. A package that needs one is reported as a warning; review licenses count as allowed for licenses.not-allowed.

[licenses]
review = ["LGPL-*"]

Keys: [licenses] review.

docs.title: licenses.not-allowed
docs.text:
Every package can be used under the licenses the policy allows.

Key: [licenses] allow. When given, a package fails unless its license can be satisfied with allow and review licenses alone. An -or-later requirement accepts later versions of the same license.

[licenses]
allow = ["MIT", "BSD-3-Clause", "Apache-2.0"]

Keys: [licenses] allow, [licenses] review.

docs.title: licenses.unknown
docs.text:
Every package declares an SPDX license.

Key: [licenses] unknown = "warn" (default), "error" or "allow": what a package with no license, or one that is not an SPDX expression, gets. pixi.lock records no PyPI licenses, so every PyPI package is unknown until pixi-policy reads license files.

[licenses]
unknown = "error"

Keys: [licenses] unknown.

docs.title: manifest.wildcard-spec
docs.text:
No dependency is given as *.

Key: [manifest] wildcard-spec (on once [manifest] exists). Fails a conda or PyPI dependency given as "*" in any dependency table, at its line in the manifest.

[manifest]
wildcard-spec = true

Keys: [manifest] wildcard-spec.

docs.title: manifest.python-pinned
docs.text:
Python is constrained to one minor version or narrower.

Key: [manifest] python-pinned (on once [manifest] exists). Fails a python dependency whose spec allows more than one minor version (">=3.10"), or has none; "3.12.*" and ">=3.12,<3.13" pass.

[manifest]
python-pinned = true

Keys: [manifest] python-pinned.

docs.title: manifest.required-platforms
docs.text:
The workspace lists every platform the policy requires.

Key: [manifest] required-platforms, a list of platforms the workspace must list in [workspace] platforms.

[manifest]
required-platforms = ["linux-64", "osx-arm64"]

Keys: [manifest] required-platforms.

docs.title: lock.present
docs.text:
The workspace has a pixi.lock.

Key: [lock] present (on once [lock] exists). Fails a workspace without a pixi.lock; without [lock], a missing lockfile is an input error (exit 2) instead.

[lock]
present = true

Keys: [lock] present.

docs.title: lock.complete
docs.text:
Every environment is locked for every platform it is solved for.

Key: [lock] complete (on once [lock] exists). Fails an environment the manifest defines that pixi.lock does not lock, or does not lock for one of its platforms.

[lock]
complete = true

Keys: [lock] complete.

docs.title: lock.in-sync
docs.text:
pixi.lock still satisfies the manifest.

Key: [lock] in-sync (on once [lock] exists). Asks pixi, offline, whether pixi.lock still satisfies the manifest (pixi list --locked); a warning when pixi cannot be run.

[lock]
in-sync = true

Keys: [lock] in-sync.

docs.title: waivers.expired
docs.text:
A waiver has expired, and what it waived fails again.

A [[waivers]] entry whose expires date has passed. What it waived fails again; renew it with a new date and a reason that still holds, or fix the finding.

[[waivers]]
rule = "licenses.deny"
package = "readline"
reason = "dev only; LEGAL-1234"
expires = 2027-03-31

Keys: [[waivers]] expires.

docs.title: waivers.unused
docs.text:
A waiver matches no finding.

A [[waivers]] entry that matches no finding: its rule, package, version, environment or platform is wrong, or the finding is gone. Remove it.

[[waivers]]
rule = "bans.deny"
package = "pycrypto"
reason = "replaced in Q3"
expires = 2027-01-31

Keys: [[waivers]] rule, [[waivers]] package, [[waivers]] version, [[waivers]] environment, [[waivers]] platform.

docs.title: waivers.too-long
docs.text:
A waiver runs further out than max-waiver-days.

A [[waivers]] entry whose expires is more than max-waiver-days (default 365) away. The waiver still applies. Set max-waiver-days at the top of the policy; 0 turns the check off.

max-waiver-days = 180

Keys: max-waiver-days, [[waivers]] expires.

docs.title: Waivers
docs.text:
A waiver is an exception for one rule and one package, with a reason and an end date. The waived finding is still reported, as waived, and does not fail the check. The day after expires, it fails again.

[[waivers]]
rule = "licenses.deny"
package = "readline"
reason = "dev only; LEGAL-1234"
expires = 2027-03-31

docs.title: What a waiver matches
docs.text:
A waiver covers a finding when its rule and package match the finding's (the package name ignoring case), and each of version, environment and platform that it gives matches too. Leave those out to cover every version, environment and platform:

[[waivers]]
rule = "bans.deny"
package = "openssl"
version = "1.1.1w"
environment = "legacy"
platform = "linux-64"
reason = "the legacy environment ships to RHEL 7 until it is retired"
expires = 2026-12-31

Only findings about a package can be waived. The lock rules name no package; turn one off with its key ([lock] in-sync = false) instead. The findings about waivers themselves (waivers.*) cannot be waived.

docs.title: Every waiver ends
docs.text:
expires is required, as a TOML date, YYYY-MM-DD, unquoted. The policy reports three things about waivers, all as warnings at the waiver's line in the policy:

Rule When What to do waivers.expired expires has passed; what it waived fails again fix the finding, or renew the waiver with a new date and a reason that still holds waivers.unused it matches no finding remove it, or correct its rule, package, version, environment or platform waivers.too-long expires is more than max-waiver-days away (365 by default) bring expires closer, or raise max-waiver-days

max-waiver-days sets how far out a waiver may run; it is a top-level key, so it goes above the first table. 0 turns the check off:

max-waiver-days = 180

[licenses]
deny = ["GPL-3.0-*"]

docs.title: Moving from pixi-sbom's --ignore-license
docs.text: pixi-sbom's --ignore-license PACKAGE:WHY has no end date. Write each one as a waiver of licenses.deny (or licenses.not-allowed) for that package, with the reason and a date to look at it again.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
Report it privately through GitHub: Report a vulnerability (Security → Advisories → Report a vulnerability). The report is visible only to the maintainers until an advisory is published.

Please do not open a public issue for a security problem, and please do not disclose it elsewhere before a fix is out. If GitHub's form is not available to you, open a public issue asking for a private channel, with no details in it, and one will be arranged.

What to include: the version (pixi policy --version), the platform, the command you ran, and the smallest pixi.toml, pixi.lock and pixi-policy.toml that reproduce it. A crash needs a backtrace (RUST_BACKTRACE=1).

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text:
Acknowledgment Within 3 business days. This is a small project with one maintainer; if you have heard nothing after that, ping the advisory thread. Assessment Within 10 business days: whether it is in scope, how severe, and a rough fix timeline. Fix and disclosure A patch release, then a published GitHub Security Advisory with a CVE where one is warranted. Credit You are named in the advisory and the changelog unless you would rather not be. Say which you prefer.

There is no bug bounty.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: The latest release. A fix ships in the next patch release from main; there are no maintenance branches, and nothing is backported. A report against an older version is checked against the current release first.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
pixi-policy reads three files a repository's author controls, so treat each as untrusted:

  • pixi.toml, the workspace's manifest.
  • pixi.lock, the lockfile, with every package's source, version and license.
  • pixi-policy.toml, the policy itself.

It makes no network request. One rule, lock.in-sync, runs pixi list --locked offline: the pixi that started pixi policy, or the one on PATH.

In scope:

  • Memory unsafety, a panic, an unbounded allocation, or a hang on any of those inputs. The shipped binary is forbid(unsafe_code), so a memory-safety finding would almost certainly be in a dependency. Report it here anyway.
  • A file written anywhere other than the path given to --output or pixi policy init.
  • A check that passes when it should fail, in a way the author of one of those files can arrange on purpose: a banned package, a denied license or a disallowed source that is silently not reported. A policy gate an attacker can talk past is a vulnerability, not a bug.
  • Running anything other than pixi list --locked, or passing it an argument taken from the inputs unchecked.
  • Anything in the release workflow that would let a third party influence what a release contains.

Out of scope:

  • Vulnerabilities in the packages a workspace contains. pixi-policy has no advisory rules yet.
  • A wrong license in a package's own metadata, as pixi.lock records it. Report it as a normal bug if you think the lockfile is read wrongly.
  • Anything requiring an attacker who already has write access to the machine.

docs.title: Verifying a release
docs.text:
Every release archive carries a signed build-provenance attestation. To check a download came from this repository's release workflow, built from that release's tag on a GitHub-hosted runner:

gh attestation verify pixi-policy-v<version>-<platform>.tar.gz --repo aesir-oss/pixi-policy \
  --signer-workflow aesir-oss/pixi-policy/.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml \
  --source-ref refs/tags/v<version> \
  --deny-self-hosted-runners

Releases up to 0.1.0 were built, and signed, in aesir-oss/pixi-ext-contrib, tagged pixi-policy-v<version> there. They were copied to this repository's releases page with every file, including each archive's signed bundle (<archive>.sigstore.json). Verify them against that bundle, naming the repository that built them. The check runs offline and does not need that repository to exist:

gh attestation verify pixi-policy-v0.1.0-linux-64.tar.gz \
  --bundle pixi-policy-v0.1.0-linux-64.tar.gz.sigstore.json \
  --repo aesir-oss/pixi-ext-contrib \
  --signer-workflow aesir-oss/pixi-ext-contrib/.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml \
  --source-ref refs/tags/pixi-policy-v0.1.0 \
  --deny-self-hosted-runners
